subject: Next steps: hosted evaluation — endpoints, rate sizing & quickstart
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@brightcart.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation follow-up — endpoints, rate sizing & quickstart

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our demo and a short next-steps checklist so your team can run a hosted evaluation quickly: 

What we covered
- Demo: /v1/generate (chat & completion) and /v1/embeddings endpoints, streaming enabled.
- Observability: per-endpoint latency & token counters in Redwood Console.
- Deployment fit: Hosted is a fast onramp; Dedicated becomes sensible for steady high throughput or strict throughput SLAs; Private/VPC for regulated data residency.

Quickstart plan (3-day onramp) — what we can provision for you
1) Sandbox access: dedicated hosted sandbox endpoints (read-only keys)
2) Example client config + rate limits tuned to your traffic profile
3) Sample prompts & prefix/KV cache guidance to reduce token usage
4) A follow-up 30-minute session to validate traffic against the sandbox and tune batching

Questions we still need from you to tailor the sandbox:
- Target steady-state QPS (typical and peak) and average tokens per request (chat messages and embedding calls).
- Any regulatory constraints (EU data residency, PCI, HIPAA) that would push toward Private now.
- Procurement timeline for a potential Dedicated contract (if you expect >100 RPS sustained).

Rates & endpoints (starter guidance)
- Sandbox default throttle: 60 RPS across account with per-endpoint ceilings we can adjust for the trial.
- Token budget: we typically suggest a 5M token bucket for a two-week eval (we can size up/down).
- Latency SLOs: hosted median <150ms for small-completion workloads; dependent on model/seq length.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf (quick checklist + API examples).

Next steps
- If you confirm you want to start with Hosted, I’ll send sandbox creds and a suggested traffic slice to test (we can bump the RPS temporarily if you need to validate burst behavior).
- Can we lock a time Thursday or Friday for the sandbox tune session?

Thanks — looking forward to getting you started.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@brightcart.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation follow-up — endpoints, rate sizing & quickstart

Thanks, Stephanie — appreciated the recap. BrightCart is inclined to start on Hosted for speed; we expect to evaluate Dedicated in Q4 if the trial looks good. A few specifics from our side: 

Traffic profile (approx):
- Peak burst: ~220 RPS (cart checkout spike windows)
- Steady-state: ~85 RPS during business hours
- Payload mix: ~65% chat (avg ~150 tokens per message), ~30% embeddings (multi-embedding calls for product vectors), ~5% rerank requests (short prompts)
- Monthly token estimate (trial window projection): ~80M tokens

Compliance/residency
- We need EU data residency for EU users; for the pilot it's OK to route EU traffic to our EU region later — not a blocker for starting Hosted in US for our internal QA.

Questions for Redwood
1) Can Hosted sandbox support validating 220 RPS bursts, or do we need a Dedicated preview?
2) If we start Hosted and later move to Dedicated, how seamless is the migration (DNS/endpoint changes, keys)?
3) Any recommended token-budget guardrails we should apply in client SDKs to prevent runaway cost during the trial?

Procurement: procurement is not blocking the pilot, but for Dedicated we’ll need a standard SOW and cost estimate. 

If you can send sandbox creds today, we’ll try to run a short stress test tomorrow and sync after. Thursday 10am PT or Friday 11am PT works for a tune session.

— Sarah
Sarah Cole
Head of ML Platform, BrightCart
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@brightcart.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation follow-up — endpoints, rate sizing & quickstart

Hi Sarah — copying Karthik for infra details. Quick answers and pragmatic next steps: 

1) Burst validation on Hosted
- Short answer: yes — we can temporarily increase the hosted sandbox ceiling to validate 220 RPS bursts for short windows (15-30 minutes) to test behavior. For repeated bursts at that level, Dedicated is more predictable.
- Mechanism: we’ll provision a sandbox slice with a raised per-endpoint QPS and token bucket for the stress run; we request a 30-minute heads-up before the test.

2) Migration path (Hosted -> Dedicated)
- Seamless from an API standpoint: no application code changes required (same endpoints & SDK), we provide DNS aliases and a migration playbook.
- Keys & rollout: you’ll receive new keys for Dedicated; we recommend a canary switch in DNS and a small traffic slice first. See attached deployment-transition-playbook.pdf for the step-by-step.

3) Client guardrails to control token spend
- Token caps per user/session: enforce soft caps at the SDK layer (e.g., max 1,000 tokens per interaction) and a global per-minute token budget monitored via our Console.
- Prefix/KV cache guidance: use short-term KV caching for repeated prompts (we expect ~30% token savings in chat-heavy flows).

Sizing & cost guidance (ballpark for planning)
- For steady 85 RPS with your mix, we recommend a hosted eval slice with: 200 RPS peak allowance, 10M token/day bucket during the trial.
- If you see sustained 200+ RPS for >72 hours, we should discuss Dedicated capacity.
- Cost note (pilot estimate only): hosted unit economics will vary by model; we’ll provide an evaluation quote once we know model choice & exact token volume.

Attachments: rateplan-matrix.csv (suggested throttle & token buckets for common trial sizes).

Next steps (proposed)
- Stephanie: provision sandbox keys with temporary raised burst ceiling.
- Sarah: confirm which day/time you want the stress run (Thursday 10am PT preferred by BrightCart).
- Karthik/aditya: join the tune session to help interpret Console metrics and adjust prefix/KV cache settings.

We’ll also add a short health-check checklist to the sandbox access email to help you validate latency and error behavior during bursts.

— Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Talk on Thursday.
